strategy.summary: A mechanical London Killzone trading plan designed to synchronize lower-timeframe execution with a higher-timeframe move from a premium array to a discount array. Price is entered in London on an overlapping fair value gap or ST model structure, with the stop loss placed above an intermediate term high that covers higher-timeframe imbalances.

timeframes.notes: The strategy pairs a 4-hour PD array with a 5-minute execution timeframe. When utilizing Daily PD arrays, the entry timeframe must be scaled upward accordingly. The 5-minute chart must be aligned with 15-minute and 1-hour context.

other: Price reacting from an HTF (4-hour) premium array targeting an opposing HTF discount array (swing low).

glossary.ST MODEL: An entry pattern involving two consecutive same-direction fair value gaps: price forms a first FVG, retraces into it, and subsequently prints a second FVG to trigger entry.
glossary.INTERMEDIATE TERM HIGH: A structural swing high that has no higher-timeframe (15m or 1h) unfilled fair value gaps hovering above it, ensuring price has no institutional reason to revisit that level.
glossary.OVERLAPPING PD ARRAY: A confluence zone where a newly formed entry-timeframe FVG directly overlaps with a pre-existing higher or lower timeframe PD array.

custom_signals.name: asia_expansion
custom_signals.plain_definition: Asian session expands away from the HTF PD array leaving fair value gaps in its leg, indicating that London will deliver continuation rather than sweeping Asian highs/lows.

custom_signals.name: asia_consolidation
custom_signals.plain_definition: Asian session remains in a tight range without expansion, requiring London to create the extreme of the day and print the ST model (two consecutive FVGs) before reversing.

custom_signals.name: st_model_entry
custom_signals.plain_definition: A two-stage displacement pattern where price forms a first FVG, retraces into it, and forms a second same-direction FVG, confirming order flow alignment.

custom_signals.name: intermediate_term_high_stop
custom_signals.plain_definition: A swing high that has no higher timeframe (15m or 1h) fair value gaps hovering directly above it.

custom_signals.name: overlapping_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: A confluence zone where a new entry-timeframe FVG overlaps with an existing higher or lower timeframe PD array.

sequence: Identify an HTF (4-hour) premium array (order block or bearish FVG) and define the draw on liquidity at the opposing 4-hour discount array (swing low) [00:41, 01:10].
Observe Asian session price action to determine whether it expands away with FVGs or consolidates [01:24, 05:27].
At London session open (02:00 NY local time), monitor the 5-minute timeframe for alignment with the 4-hour directional bias [01:24, 01:54].
Scenario A (Asia Expansion): If Asia expanded lower leaving bearish FVGs, wait for London to create a new 5-minute bearish fair value gap, then enter short on the overlapping PD array [01:40, 02:03].

Scenario B (Asia Consolidation): If Asia consolidated, wait for London to tap the premium array, form a first bearish FVG, retrace into it, and print a second bearish FVG (the ST model) before entering short [04:52, 05:09].
Inspect the 15-minute and 1-hour timeframes to confirm whether any fair value gaps hover above the local swing high [02:36, 02:42].
Place the stop loss above the intermediate term high that covers all overhead 15m/1h imbalances [02:54, 03:02].
Target the opposing 4-hour swing low discount array [01:17, 03:08].

invalidation.text: The setup is invalidated if price closes above the intermediate term high chosen for stop loss placement.
Do not place a tight stop loss immediately above a 5-minute high if an unmitigated 15-minute or 1-hour fair value gap hovers above it.

filters.text: Focus primarily on Forex pairs; indices have different characteristics and require a separate strategy.
Do not use a 5-minute entry timeframe when executing off Daily PD arrays; scale up the entry timeframe for higher-timeframe arrays.
The entry timeframe must always be traded in context with the timeframes directly above it (5m in concert with 15m and 1h).

entry_rule.text: In London, enter on an overlapping PD array upon the creation of a new bearish fair value gap (or after the second FVG in the ST model).
entry_rule.quote: all I need to see in London is a new bearish fair value Gap then I enter on the overlapping PD array

target_rule.text: Target the opposing 4-hour discount array, specifically the 4-hour swing low.
target_rule.quote: what is our Target our Target is this swing low on the four hour that is your discount rate

stop_rule.text: Place the stop loss above the intermediate term high that covers any overhead 15-minute or 1-hour fair value gaps.
stop_rule.quote: you cover these highs price has no reason to come back there which on the 5 minutes is this intermediate term high

management.notes: A re-entry is valid if price produces another bearish FVG and establishes a new intermediate term high, targeting the same 4-hour discount low.

presenter_claims.claim: All concepts including AMD, Power of 3, Midnight Open, New Week Opening Gap, Enigma, and Reaper are inherently integrated into this simple trading plan without needing to track them individually.
The hard work is done on the higher timeframe; on the lower timeframe you are merely getting in sync.

strategy.notes: The trading plan establishes mechanical guidelines for London Killzone trading. Whether Asia expands or consolidates does not invalidate the trade; it simply dictates whether one enters on the continuation FVG or waits for the ST model two-FVG sequence.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price pushes up to form an intermediate term high that covers higher timeframe FVGs.
Strong bearish displacement creates a new 5m bearish fair value gap during the London Killzone.
Price retraces into the newly formed London FVG, mitigating it and triggering the short entry.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter highlights that because Asia expanded downward and created its own FVGs, we simply wait for London to print a continuation FVG. He heavily emphasizes placing the stop above an 'intermediate term high' that protects against unmitigated 15m/1h arrays, rather than the immediate 5m swing high.

may_differ.reason: Presenter uses 'overlapping PD array' loosely without strictly defining if it's an OB or FVG on the exact same timeframe.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price displaces lower to form the first bearish FVG after tapping the 4-hour premium array.
Price retraces into the first bearish FVG.
Price displaces down a second time, leaving a second bearish FVG.
Price retraces into the second FVG, mitigating it and triggering the ST model short entry.
